name: 5PB1108PGGI
title: 5PB11xx family: 1.8 V to 3.3 V LVCMOS clock fanout buffers, 1:2 to 1:10, 200 MHz
summary: A family of LVCMOS clock buffers that copy one input clock to 2, 4, 6, 8 or 10 outputs (5PB1102 to 5PB1110; 5PB1108PGGI is the 1:8 part in a 16-pin TSSOP, industrial grade). It runs from a 1.71 V to 3.465 V supply, takes inputs up to 200 MHz on a 3.3 V tolerant input, and adds under 50 fs RMS of phase jitter. Each output has about 50 Ω of series termination built in, and a single enable pin turns all outputs on or off without runt pulses. Packages are 8- to 20-pin TSSOP, 2 × 2 mm DFN and 2.5 × 2.5 mm and 3 × 3 mm VFQFPN, in industrial, extended and AEC-Q100 automotive grades.
key_figures: 0.05 ps RMS max, 156.25 MHz, 12 kHz to 20 MHz

circuits.title: Test load
circuits.description: The load every output is measured into: the output drives a 50 Ω line five inches long, ended in a 5 pF capacitor to ground.
notes: Y0 stands for any output.

operation.text: Five fanout widths share one design: 5PB1102 (two outputs), 5PB1104 (four), 5PB1106 (six), 5PB1108 (eight) and 5PB1110 (ten). One LVCMOS input, CLKIN, feeds every output through a buffer, and one enable pin, 1G, gates all outputs together.

The part runs from 1.8 V, 2.5 V or 3.3 V nominal (1.71 V to 3.465 V). CLKIN accepts a 3.3 V clock even when VDD is lower; its absolute limit is 3.63 V regardless of VDD. The CLKIN thresholds scale with VDD (0.7 × VDD high, 0.3 × VDD low) while the 1G thresholds are fixed per supply.

With 1G low every output sits low. Raising or lowering 1G takes effect within three input clock cycles, and the change is glitch-free: no intermediate incorrect output cycle appears during the transition, so the downstream device sees no frequency peaking.

Each output has about 50 Ω of series termination built in, matched to a 50 Ω trace. Output duty cycle follows the input; it equals the input duty cycle when the CLKIN high level reaches VDD. Outputs are valid within 3 ms of the supply ramp (3.2 ms for 5PB1110NDG2 at 1.8 V).

Measured on a 100 MHz carrier with a 12 kHz to 20 MHz integration band, the reference source showed about 58.9 fs RMS phase jitter and the buffer output about 70.9 fs, an additive jitter of 39 fs. The specified limit is 0.05 ps RMS at 156.25 MHz for industrial and extended parts; automotive parts are 0.05 ps to 0.06 ps (5PB1104) and 0.065 ps to 0.068 ps (5PB1110) depending on supply.

Industrial parts (suffix I) run from -40 °C to +85 °C and extended parts (suffix K) from -40 °C to +105 °C. 5PB1104CMG1 and 5PB1104CMT1 are AEC-Q100 Grade 1 (-40 °C to +125 °C); 5PB1110NDG2 is AEC-Q100 Grade 2 (-40 °C to +105 °C). CMT and the automotive NDG parts have wettable flanks.

TSSOP parts in 14, 16 and 20 pins carry IDT5PB11 on the first line and the device digits with package and grade code (for example 08PGGI) on the second, then a date code YYWW and mark code $$. The 8-TSSOP shows B11AAI or B11AAK under a stepping and date line, where AA is the device number (02 or 04). The 16-VFQFPN shows 1106 or 1108 (industrial) or 106K or 108K (extended) over Y and a lot sequence. The 8-DFN shows 11AA (industrial) or 1AAK (extended) over YW and a lot sequence; the automotive 8-DFN shows 1041 (CMG1) or 104W (CMT1 wettable flank). The 20-VFQFPN shows a three-character assembly lot code, YWW$, and 110I, 110K or 1102. G after the package code means RoHS compliant.

A trailing 8 means tape and reel. The /W option is tape and reel with EIA-481-D pin-1 orientation; other reels use EIA-481-C. A special material request adds a /X code to the standard number (for example 5PB1104CMGI/X).
